title: Affordance Garden — idea log
content:
Quick notepad for the 'Affordance Garden' concept — a sandbox of small, composable affordances (micro-features) we can expose to product teams to shape runtime behavior without full rollout complexity.

Context / motivation:
- Teams keep asking for easy knobs to trade cost/latency vs fidelity (not always full rollout).
- Current fallback lanes are coarse: model A -> model B. Hard to express nuanced, localized affordances (e.g., shorten recap only for low-value chats).
- Want a small surface that product engineers can mix-and-match (toggles + lightweight rules) and get predictable econ impact.

Rough concept:
- Affordance = tiny behavioral modifier applied at request-time or session-time. Examples: 'aggressive-trim', 'compact-recap', 'bias-for-safety', 'embed-first-lookup'.
- Each affordance has metadata: likely token delta (est), expected latency delta, quality vector (user-visible dims), fallback severity.
- Affordances composed by precedence rules (user-level, route-level, session-presets).

User stories (trying to keep atomic):
- As a product engineer, I want to add 'compact-recap' to a chat route so that low-value sessions use fewer tokens, keeping core accuracy for follow-ups.
- As a support engineer, I want to see which affordances fired on a failing request to correlate regressions with micro-changes.
- As a PM, I want a quick estimate of cost savings if 30% of requests enable 'aggressive-trim'.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Config UI/JSON route field to toggle up to 3 affordances per route.
- Runtime hook that maps affordance -> pre-configured prompt fragment + routing hint (model variant or max tokens).
- Telemetry: token usage delta and affordance tag on traces/logs.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Keep affordances purely additive to avoid combinatorial policy explosion: base prompt + ordered fragments.
- Leverage existing routing policies: affordance can request 'lower-cost-variant' but must be optional (not hard redirect).
- Prefill suggested fragments and token ests from model bench (see LIN-847 experiment data).

Experiment plan (cheap iterations):
1) Internal alpha: pick two routes (support chat + search-assist). Add 2 affordances: compact-recap, low-temp-fallback. Run for 2 weeks for 10% traffic. Measure per-request token delta and CSAT delta (pilot).
2) Customer pilot: invite 2 small customers on Dedicated to try; collect qualitative feedback and redlines.

Metrics to track:
- per-request token delta (primary econ metric)
- latency p95 impact
- %requests with affordance active
- QA signal: task success / CSAT (sampled)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to version affordance fragments? (tie to model version or independent?)
- UI: quick-choose vs JSON rules. Need designs. @Mira will mock.
- Safety: ensure 'aggressive-trim' can't be applied to system-critical routes by default. Need default denylist.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Could map affordances to a small 'safety budget' token pool per session to allow occasional expensive generations while normally enforcing compactness.
- Consider lightweight eval harness: golden prompts + affordance runs to estimate drift. Put under micro-evals (maybe reuse emilia's sketches).

References / links: see LIN-847 for the bench numbers that inform token estimates; linked PR shows initial runtime hook prototype.

Next steps:
- Sync with Mira + infra lead to validate telemetry delta.
- Draft sketch for Console quick-actions (one-click apply + preview cost delta).
- Build alpha toggle & runtime flag for 10% traffic router.

Random thoughts (loosely related):
- 'Affordance marketplace' where product teams can share vetted fragments (maybe later).
- Short-hand affordance presets (economy / balanced / fidelity) that map to sets of affordances.

End of pad. This is messy, will prune into PRD if we get buy-in.
